The full dataset has no such file, and every\n    # session the index lists is on disk.\n    # Compare in string space: one.search returns UUID objects while the csv column\n    # is str, so a plain set intersection is empty whatever the contents. keep must\n    # stay UUID-valued for the `eid in keep` test below.\n    if subset_csv is not None:\n        subset_eids = set(pd.read_csv(subset_csv).eid.astype(str))\n        keep = {eid for eid in keep if str(eid) in subset_eids}\n        if not keep:\n            raise SystemExit(f'No sessions matched {subset_csv}; refusing to continue.')\n\n    eids, info = one.search(query_type='local', details=True)\n    selected = {}\n    for eid, session in zip(eids, info):\n        if eid in keep:\n            selected.setdefault(session['subject'], []).append(str(eid))\n    return {subject: selected[subject] for subject in sorted(selected)}\n\n\ndef camera_view(eid):\n    \"\"\"The side camera this session has whisker motion energy for, left preferred.\"\"\"\n    for view in ('left', 'right'):\n        if len(one.list_datasets(eid, filename=f'{view}Camera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                 query_type='local')):\n            return view\n    raise ValueError(f'no whisker motion energy for {eid}')\n\n\n# --- trials ---\n\ndef trial_variables(trials):\n    \"\"\"Choice, block prior and trial number in block, one row per trial.\"\"\"\n    # probabilityLeft is constant within a block, so a change of value starts a new block\n    block = (trials.probabilityLeft != trials.probabilityLeft.shift()).cumsum()\n\n    return pd.DataFrame({'choice': trials.choice.map(CHOICE),\n                         'prior': trials.probabilityLeft.map(PRIOR),\n                         'trial_in_block': trials.groupby(block).cumcount()})\n\n\ndef covered(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Trials whose window is spanned by this stream, allowing the one bin gap the reference allows.\"\"\"\n    start, stop = stim_on + T_START, stim_on + T_STOP\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, start, side='right')      # first sample inside the window\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, stop, side='left') - 1       # last sample inside the window\n\n    # a trial with no sample at all, or a gap at either edge, has no usable trace\n    inside = begin <= end\n    first = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\n    last = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\n    return inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n\n\ndef usable_trials(trials, wheel_times, camera_times):\n    \"\"\"Trials the paper would keep, that also have a full wheel and camera window.\"\"\"\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()\n    reaction = trials.firstMovement_times.to_numpy() - stim_on\n\n    keep = (reaction >= MIN_RT) & (reaction <= MAX_RT)          # NaN compares false, so those go too\n    keep &= trials.choice.isin(CHOICE).to_numpy()               # drops the no response trials\n    keep &= trials.probabilityLeft.isin(PRIOR).to_numpy()\n\n    return keep & covered(wheel_times, stim_on) & covered(camera_times, stim_on)\n\n\n# --- behavior ---\n\ndef window_slice(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Index range of each trial window, so a stream is sliced rather than rescanned per trial.\"\"\"\n    window_start = stim_on + T_START\n    window_stop = stim_on + T_STOP\n\n    # the samples are in time order, so each window is one contiguous range of them\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, window_start)\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, window_stop)\n\n    return begin, end\n\n\ndef trial_traces(times, values, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"A continuous trace resampled onto the same time grid for every trial.\"\"\"\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    traces = []\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        # one sample either side of the window, so the first and last bin centre are\n        # interpolated rather than clamped to the nearest sample inside it\n        first = max(begin[trial] - 1, 0)\n        last = end[trial] + 1\n\n        traces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n\n    return np.array(traces)\n\n\ndef discretize(trace):\n    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's own trace.\"\"\"\n    return np.digitize(trace, np.percentile(trace, SPLIT))\n\n\n# --- neural ---\n\ndef load_neural(eid):\n    \"\"\"Spike times and good clusters of a session, merged over its probes.\"\"\"\n    times, units, regions = [], [], []\n    for pid, name in zip(*one.eid2pid(eid)):\n        loader = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=pid, one=one, eid=eid, pname=name)\n\n        # skip the md5 check, which rereads every spike file and draws its own progress bar\n        spikes, clusters, channels = loader.load_spike_sorting(check_hash=False)\n\n        # a session can hold an insertion whose spike sorting was never released\n        if not clusters:\n            continue\n\n        clusters = loader.merge_clusters(spikes, clusters, channels)   # attaches metrics and histology\n\n        # `void` is the atlas label for a channel the histology placed outside the brain,\n        # so a unit there is not in a brain region at all\n        in_brain = brain_regions.acronym2acronym(\n            clusters['acronym'], mapping='Beryl') != 'void'\n\n        # spikes.clusters holds the row of the cluster table, so a per cluster flag\n        # can be indexed by it directly to say whether each spike survives\n        is_good = (clusters['label'] >= QC_LABEL) & in_brain\n        keep = is_good[spikes['clusters']]\n\n        # renumber the surviving clusters, continuing the count from the previous probe\n        new_index = np.cumsum(is_good) - 1\n        units.append(new_index[spikes['clusters'][keep]] + len(regions))\n        times.append(spikes['times'][keep])\n\n        # Beryl is the coarser atlas the reference code uses, e.g. DG-sg and DG-mo both become DG\n        regions.extend(brain_regions.acronym2acronym(clusters['acronym'][is_good], mapping='Beryl'))\n\n    times, units = np.concatenate(times), np.concatenate(units)\n\n    # sort the merged probes by spike time, as the reference does, so trials can be sliced\n    order = np.argsort(times, kind='stable')\n    return times[order], units[order], np.array(regions)\n\n\ndef spike_counts(times, units, n_units, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Spike count per unit and bin, for every trial.\"\"\"\n    counts = np.empty((stim_on.size, n_units, N_BINS))\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        spike_time = times[begin[trial]:end[trial]] - onset      # time from stimulus onset\n        spike_unit = units[begin[trial]:end[trial]]\n\n        bin_index = np.floor((spike_time - T_START) / BIN).astype(np.int64)\n        \n        # a spike sitting on the window edge can round out of range once the onset is subtracted\n        bin_index = np.clip(bin_index, 0, N_BINS - 1)\n\n        # one flat index per spike lets a single bincount fill the whole unit by bin grid\n        flat_index = spike_unit * N_BINS + bin_index\n        counts[trial] = np.bincount(flat_index, minlength=n_units * N_BINS).reshape(n_units, N_BINS)\n\n    return counts\n\n\n# --- session ---\n\ndef process_session(eid, subject):\n    \"\"\"One session as loader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n\n    trials, wheel = loader.trials, loader.wheel\n    motion_energy = loader.motion_energy[f'{view}Camera']\n\n    variables = trial_variables(trials)                 # before filtering, so the block count is real\n    keep = usable_trials(trials, wheel.times.to_numpy(), motion_energy.times.to_numpy())\n    variables = variables[keep]\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()[keep]\n\n    # no trial survived the mask, so there is nothing to load or bin\n    if stim_on.size == 0:\n        return {'session_id': str(eid), 'subject': subject, 'camera': view,\n                'neural': [], 'input': [], 'output': [],\n                'n_trials': 0, 'n_units': 0, 'regions': np.array([])}\n\n    speed = trial_traces(wheel.times, np.abs(wheel.velocity), stim_on)\n    whisker = trial_traces(motion_energy.times, motion_energy.iloc[:, 1], stim_on)\n\n    spike_times, spike_units, regions = load_neural(eid)\n    rate = spike_counts(spike_times, spike_units, regions.size, stim_on) / BIN\n\n    # the split is over the whole session, so both traces are discretized once, not per trial\n    speed_class = discretize(speed)\n    whisker_class = discretize(whisker)\n\n    neural = [trial.astype(np.float32) for trial in rate]\n    inputs, outputs = [], []\n    for trial in range(stim_on.size):\n        row = variables.iloc[trial]\n        inputs.append(np.stack([TIME, np.full(N_BINS, row.trial_in_block)]).astype(np.float32))\n        outputs.append(np.stack([np.full(N_BINS, row.choice),          'neural': neural, 'input': inputs, 'output': outputs,\n            'n_trials': len(neural), 'n_units': regions.size, 'regions': regions}\n\n\ndef assemble(results):\n    \"\"\"Stitch per-session results into the target dictionary.\"\"\"\n    subjects = sorted({r['subject'] for r in results})\n    sub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subjects)}\n\n    regions = sorted({region for r in results for region in r['regions']})\n    reg_ix = {region: i for i, region in enumerate(regions)}\n\n    return {\n        'neural': [r['neural'] for r in results],\n        'input': [r['input'] for r in results],\n        'output': [r['output'] for r in results],\n\n        'subjects': subjects,\n        'subject_idx': np.array([sub_ix[r['subject']] for r in results], np.int32),\n\n        'brain_regions': regions,\n        'brain_region_idx': [np.array([reg_ix[x] for x in r['regions']], np.int32) for r in results],\n\n        'input_names': INPUT_NAMES,\n        'output_names': OUTPUT_NAMES,\n        'output_values': OUTPUT_VALUES,\n\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Convert the IBL Brain-Wide Map dataset into the decoder-ready pickle format.\n\nUsage\n-----\n    python -u /app/convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--show-processing]\n\nProcessing follows the reference caching pipeline of Zhang et al. 2026\n(`/app/code/code_zhang2025/src/0_data_caching.py` + `src/utils/ibl_data_utils.py`):\n\n    params = {'interval_len': 2, 'binsize': 0.02, 'single_region': False,\n              'align_time': 'stimOn_times', 'time_window': (-.5, 1.5)}\n\ni.e. trials aligned to stimulus onset, a 2 s window from -0.5 s to +1.5 s, binned into\n100 non-overlapping 20 ms bins, with all neurons of a session Implemented here\n    with a single `np.bincount` over all trials instead of a per-trial multiprocessing\n    pool, which is ~100x faster and produces bit-identical counts (verified in Step 10).\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    spike_times : (n_spikes,) sorted ascending\n    spike_clusters : (n_spikes,) int in [0, n_clusters)\n    n_clusters : int\n    t_begs : (n_trials,) window start times\n\n    Returns\n    -------\n    (n_trials, n_clusters, N_BINS) float32 spike counts\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(t_begs)\n    t_ends = t_begs + N_BINS * BINSIZE\n\n    i0 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, t_begs, side='left')\n    i1 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, t_ends, side='left')\n    counts = np.maximum(i1 - i0, 0)\n    total = int(counts.sum())\n\n    binned = np.zeros((n_trials, n_clusters, N_BINS), dtype=np.float32)\n    if total == 0:\n        return binned\n\n    # Gather the spike indices of every trial window into one flat array. Tertile edges are computed from all binned values of the session, so the\n    three classes are equally populated and the balanced-accuracy chance level is exactly\n    1/3. three *release* tables are staged in\nsubdirectories (`Brainwidemap`, `2022_Q4_IBL_et_al_BWM`, `2025_Q3_IBL_et_al_BWM`).\nNone of them index the dataset **revisions actually present on disk**, e.g. the trials\ntable lives at `alf/#2025-03-03#/_ibl_trials.table.pqt` for all 459 sessions and the\nwhisker motion energy at `alf/#2025-05-29#/...`, revisions absent from every staged table.\nLoading with those tables silently returns a trials table with a *single* column\n(`goCueTrigger_times`) and raises `KeyError: 'ROIMotionEnergy'` for motion energy.\n\nFix (`/app/build_one_cache.py`): index the files that are on disk with ONE's own\nindexer `one.alf.cache.make_parquet_db`, then restore the genuine Alyx session UUIDs\n(`make_parquet_db` hashes paths into fake UUIDs) by matching `lab/subject/date/number`\nagainst the staged release tables. `default_revision` is set to the newest revision of\neach (session, collection, filename). Result: 459 sessions / 18,450 datasets written to\n`/app/data/one_cache/{sessions,datasets}.pqt`, which a plain `ONE(cache_dir=...)` picks\nup. 2 of the 461 session folders on disk (cortexlab KS074 2021-11-22, KS075 2021-12-09)\nare not in any release table and not in `bwm_release.csv`; they are dropped.\nAll data access after this step is through the `ONE` API and the `brainbox` loaders.\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Reference Code Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nReference code: `/app/code/code_zhang2025` (Zhang et al. 2026, *Neuron*), plus `ibllib`.\nThe relevant pipeline is `src/0_data_caching.py` → `src/utils/ibl_data_utils.py`.\n\n### Key Functions Identified\n| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |\n|----------|------|-------|---------|\n| `prepare_data(one, eid, bwm_df, params)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | LOADING | Per session: `one.eid2pid`, load each probe's spike sorting, merge probes, load trials+mask, load \"anytime\" behaviours. Returns `neural_dict`, `behave_dict`, `meta_data`, `trials_data`. |\n| `load_spiking_data(one, pid, qc=None)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | LOADING/CURATION | `SpikeSortingLoader(pid).load_spike_sorting()` + `merge_clusters()`. `qc=None` (the default used by `prepare_data`) keeps **all** clusters; `qc=1` would keep only `label >= 1`. `meta_data['good_clusters'] = (label >= 1)` is stored either way. |\n| `merge_probes(spikes_list, clusters_list)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | LOADING | Concatenate probes of one session into a single population (re-indexes `spikes['clusters']`, sorts by spike time). |\n| `load_trials_and_mask(one, eid, min_rt=0.08, max_rt=2., nan_exclude='default', max_trial_len=10.0, exclude_nochoice=True)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | CURATION | Trials table + boolean inclusion mask. |\n| `list_brain_regions` / `select_brain_regions` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Map cluster acronyms to the **Beryl** atlas mapping; with `single_region=False` returns one group containing every region (i.e. decode from all neurons). |\n| `bin_spiking_data(reg_clu_ids, neural_df, trials_df, **params)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Builds intervals `[align_time + t0, align_time + t1]` per trial, bins spikes with `bincount2D(xbin=binsize, xlim=[t_beg, t_end])`, truncates to `n_bins = ceil(interval_len/binsize)`. Returns `(n_trials, n_bins, n_clusters)`. |\n| `load_target_behavior(one, eid, target)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | LOADING | `SessionLoader.load_wheel()` → `wheel-speed` = `abs(velocity)`; `SessionLoader.load_motion_energy(views=[...])` → `whiskerMotionEnergy`. |\n| `get_behavior_per_interval(...)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Slices the behaviour trace to each trial interval and `interp1d`-interpolates it onto `np.linspace(t_beg + binsize, t_end, n_bins)`. Marks a trial bad if the trace is absent, starts >1 bin late, ends >1 bin early, or the interval is NaN. |\n| `bin_behaviors(one, eid, behaviors, trials_df, **params)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Per-trial task variables (`choice`, `block = probabilityLeft`, `reward`, `contrast`) + binned dynamic behaviours. |\n| `align_spike_behavior(binned_spikes, binned_behaviors, beh_names, trials_mask)` | `utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | CURATION | Drops trials failing the trials mask **or** having no valid behaviour interpolation, for spikes and every behaviour jointly. |\n| `standardize_spike_data` | `utils/data_loader_utils.py` | PROCESSING | z-scores spike counts per time bin, *inside the model's data loader* (not part of the cached dataset). |\n| `MultiRegionDataModule.list_regions` | `utils/data_loader_utils.py` | CURATION | Excludes `root` and `void` from the usable region list. |\n\n### Reference parameters (`src/0_data_caching.py`)\n```python\nparams = {'interval_len': 2, 'binsize': 0.02, 'single_region': False,\n          'align_time': 'stimOn_times', 'time_window': (-.5, 1.5)}\nbeh_names = ['choice', 'reward', 'block', 'wheel-speed', 'whisker-motion-energy']\n```\ni.e. **align to `stimOn_times`, window (−0.5, +1.5) s, 20 ms bins → T = 100** — exactly\nwhat the decoder task here asks for.\n\n### Notes on the two questions posed in the brief\n- This is **electrophysiology**, so no ΔF/F is needed.\n- **Cell quality filtering**: yes. `clusters['label']` is the fraction of the three RIGOR\n  single-unit metrics (amplitude > 50 µV, noise cutoff < 20 µV, refractory-period\n  violation) that a unit passes; `label >= 1` is the data paper's definition of a\n  \"well-isolated neuron\". The usable expectations are:\n\n| Decoded variable | Reported metric / value | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| Choice (whole session, all neurons) | accuracy ≈ 0.75–0.85 (Fig. 5B, 10 sessions); region-level balanced accuracy mostly 0.5–0.65 | methods paper Fig. 5, data paper Fig. 4 |\n| Prior | Pearson correlation ≈ 0.5–0.7 (continuous target) | methods paper Fig. 5 |\n| Wheel speed | R² ≈ 0.3–0.5 | methods paper Fig. 5C |\n| Whisker motion energy | R² ≈ 0.4–0.6 | methods paper Fig. 5D |\n| Data paper decoding | balanced accuracy, region-wise, small effect sizes over null | data paper \"Overview of decoding\" |\n\nBecause those are per-session/per-region models with continuous targets, they set the\n*order of magnitude* only. Everything is 2-D and time-varying so the per-trial\nvariables are visible to the per-timestep decoder at every step.\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Rebuild the ONE cache tables from disk** (Step 0). Without it the trials table and\n   motion energy cannot be loaded at all. The genuine eids are preserved so that\n   `bwm_release.csv`'s pid↔eid mapping — which the reference code relies on — still works\n   (`one.eid2pid` needs a live Alyx connection, which is unavailable offline).\n2. **Neurons: keep only well-isolated units (`label >= 1`) in grey matter.** The reference\n   caching script's `qc=None` keeps all 621,733 clusters, but (a) the data paper that\n   produced this dataset states its analyses use only the 75,708 well-isolated neurons and\n   explicitly restricts to grey matter, (b) the reference code still records\n   `good_clusters = label >= 1` in its metadata and its own region loader drops\n   `root`/`void`, and (c) keeping all clusters would make the converted tensor ~8× larger\n   (≈110 GB vs ≈14 GB) while adding multi-unit clusters that carry no additional\n   single-neuron signal for a PCA+linear decoder. Result: 65,301 neurons.\n3. **Window / binning: `stimOn_times`, (−0.5, +1.5) s, 20 ms, T = 100** — identical to the\n   reference caching parameters and to the decoder task specification.\n4. **Trial curation = `load_trials_and_mask` with the reference's `max_trial_len=10.0`**,\n   i.e. no NaN in {stimOn_times, choice, feedback_times, probabilityLeft,\n   firstMovement_times, feedbackType}, 0.08 s ≤ RT ≤ 2 s, trial ≤ 10 s, no no-go.\n   The unbiased block is **kept** (`exclude_unbiased=False`, the reference default),\n   because `probabilityLeft == 0.5` is one of the three required prior classes.\n5. **Trials with unusable behaviour are dropped**, using the reference's own criteria\n   (trace missing, starts more than one bin late, ends more than one bin early, NaNs) —\n   this is what `align_spike_behavior` does.\n6. **Discretisation of wheel speed / whisker ME into 3 bins: per-session tertiles**\n   (33.3rd and 66.7th percentiles of all retained binned values in that session).\n   Per-session because whisker motion energy is in arbitrary camera/ROI-dependent units\n   that are not comparable between sessions, and wheel-speed scale varies with the mouse;\n   tertiles because they give balanced classes, so the decoder's balanced accuracy has a\n   clean 1/3 chance level. Degenerate edges (ties) are handled explicitly.\n7. **Per-trial variables are broadcast across time** rather than stored as 1-D arrays, so\n   that `input` and `output` have a single consistent shape and the brief's \"if at all\n   possible, make it time-varying\" is satisfied.\n8. **Sessions with no whisker video at all are dropped** (14 of 459 → 445 sessions).\n9. Neural data are stored as raw **spike counts** (float32), not z-scored: the reference\n   z-scores inside its data loader, and `train_decoder` does its own SVD-based projection.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] Total clusters = 621,733 and good units = 75,708 across the 699 probes (paper).\n- [ ] 459 sessions, 699 pids, 139 subjects from `bwm_release.csv`.\n- [ ] Every trial has exactly T = 100 bins;
